_**User**_

i would like this tutorial to be a bit more intuitive. currently, the right sidebar is the thing doing all the explanatory heavy lifting. instead, i'd like a tutorial that slowly introduces new components of the interface. so first, it should JUST show the data on the graph so students can understand what data might be used with random forest.

Then, it should show one tree training. And say, given a new datapoint, we'd want to  know what kind of tree it is

So then the next part of the tutorial introduces a grey datapoinnt on the graph. And it should walk through ONE step of the tree and explain to the user what's happening and why that step was taken.

And then once the user understands, it should finish the tree.

Then, it should introduces the concept of multiple trees. the way it should do this is by intentionally introducing a tree that gets the wrong answer and saying, sometimes trees get the boundaries wrong. to account for this, we'll have multiple trees and have them vote. majority wins.

It should have a small text to explain each step, but nothing insanely in detail. the whole point is for the students themselves to fiddle around with random forest to learn. and in the text that you do include, absolutely ZERO em dashes

I am rewriting ForestDemo.tsx to implement the new tutorial flow.

The rewrite introduces a tutorial stage system. Each stage controls exactly which UI elements appear. Data-only appears first. Then a single tree trains. Then a misclassified tree demonstrates voting. Finally the explore stage returns full control.

The tutorial body text now adapts dynamically to each stage. It describes the first split during prediction and explains the voting mechanism during the vote phase. A helper identifies the single tree that misclassifies the query sample. Stage transitions are handled carefully to avoid unwanted resets. Auto-action effects are being added to drive the tutorial forward automatically.

Auto-effects now handle the tutorial transitions. The grow stage replays tree growth after a brief delay. The predict-step stage automatically predicts the query sample and resets the visualization state. Another effect is being wired for the predict stage.

A new `runSingleTreePathAnimation` function drives the single-tree path animation. The vote stage effect predicts the query sample, focuses the dissenting tree, and reveals the vote results. A reset effect that clears the prediction on every stage change is clashing with the tutorial state management.

The predict stage animation is now fully implemented. It runs the query sample through the first tree and advances along the decision path frame by frame until completion.

The predict-step stage now highlights the root node when the path index is zero. A new `runTutorialVoteAnimation` function reveals each tree’s vote result one by one, then triggers the merge animation once all votes are visible. The tutorial header will hide the Back and Next buttons to keep the interface minimal.

The tutorial caption will sit at the bottom of the screen, replacing the usual header navigation. During the tutorial, the header will only show a "Skip" button; in the explore stage, it will show a "Replay tutorial" button. Scatter plot selection will be disabled while the tutorial is active, except in the explore stage.

The shell layout switches to a single full-width column whenever the sidebar is hidden. The panels container also collapses to a single column during the data stage and shrinks to a 560-pixel maximum width. The tree path visualization is now enabled across every tutorial stage.

The data stage will center the scatter plot. Tutorial navigation is now fully wired: pressing Next advances through stages, and reaching the vote stage automatically finishes the tutorial and returns to explore. The app checks a dismissed flag on startup to decide whether to begin in the tutorial or jump straight to explore.

The tourOpen state is being removed entirely. The sidebar will only render when showSidebar is true. During the tutorial grow stage, the tree picker will be disabled and only tree 1 will be available. Action buttons such as walk and merge need to be moved out of the expand overlay so they remain visible in the explore stage.

The walk and merge buttons were previously only inside the expand overlay. I will add a compact toolbar visible only in the explore stage so those controls stay accessible without expanding the view.

The unused `.toolbar` CSS class will be wired into the explore-mode toolbar. During the vote stage, the tree picker will be shown so users can see multiple trees, with the dissenting tree highlighted. The ensemble merge component will receive a special query sample ID and a highlight ID for the wrong tree. The stage sidebar will hide its bullet list and tip when empty. The full ForestDemo file is ready to be written.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

The tutorial now introduces the interface step by step instead of leaning on the sidebar. Here is the new flow:

### Step 1: Data only
Just the scatter plot. Short caption explains that each dot is a labeled leaf (width vs length, color = species).

### Step 2: One tree
The tree panel appears and Tree 1 grows automatically. Caption explains that trees ask questions to classify new leaves.

### Step 3: First split
A **grey dot** appears on the graph (unknown species). The tree highlights the root split. Caption walks through that one decision (feature value, threshold, left/right).

### Step 4: Finish the tree
On Next, the path animates down to a leaf. Caption explains that the leaf's species is this tree's guess.

### Step 5: Many trees vote
Tree picker appears with all 5 trees. The dissenting tree is highlighted. Votes animate in. Caption explains that individual trees can get boundaries wrong, so the forest votes and majority wins.

### Step 6: Explore
Full UI unlocks: knobs, sidebar, toolbar, click-to-select, walk/merge buttons.

**Other changes:**
- Replaced the spotlight tour and heavy sidebar with a bottom `TutorialCaption` bar (Back / Next / Skip)
- Sidebar only shows in explore mode
- Removed the old bootstrap stage from the tutorial path
- All tutorial copy has zero em dashes

Use **Replay tutorial** in the header after finishing, or clear `forest-lab-tutorial-dismissed` in localStorage to see it again on reload.
